answer: Jade-clock admission: each identity must submit its first transaction at a scheduled offset derived from a shared atlas of epoch slots. Slots are spaced unevenly so arrival times encode identity. An agent arriving outside its assigned window is queued to the next epoch, delaying service. To flood the network with many identities, an attacker must either occupy distinct slots, paying latency per identity equal to one full epoch, or collide in a slot, which reveals the cluster. Ravens monitoring slot occupancy flag dense arrivals as probable sybils.
